lessons.title: Anchoring Phenomenon Launch — "The Matatu Horn and the Fading Radio"

quiz.prompt: On the Nakuru–Nairobi highway, a matatu in the opposite lane passes a bus at high speed while hooting. The matatu driver does not change the horn at all. What does the student on the bus hear?
choices: The horn keeps exactly the same pitch the whole time, because the driver does not change it
The horn sounds lower-pitched as the matatu approaches, then rises to a higher pitch as it moves away
The horn sounds higher-pitched as the matatu approaches, then drops to a lower pitch as it moves away
The horn changes pitch only because the driver presses the button harder as he passes
quiz.rationale: The story and the buzzer-on-a-string demonstration both show a higher pitch on approach and a sudden drop as the source moves away. Blaming the driver's button is the surface-feature idea the teacher sorts into pile B.
quiz.placement: Step 1 hook narration and Step 2 live buzzer demonstration

quiz.prompt: A student's PREDICT card has three prompts: NOTICE, PUZZLING and BEST GUESS. Which of these statements belongs under 'What did you NOTICE?'
choices: FM probably cuts out because the tunnel walls block it
Something about the wave must change when the matatu moves
The buzzer sounded higher as it swung towards me and lower as it swung away
Why does AM keep playing inside the Kabete tunnel?
quiz.rationale: A 'notice' is an observable fact about what was heard or seen. A mechanism, such as a wave changing or walls blocking, is a guess or inference, and a question beginning with 'Why' belongs under 'puzzling'.

quiz.prompt: At Station A, a student uses the PhET 'Sound' simulation. The listener stays still and the student moves the sound source towards the listener. Which perceived pitch should the student record in the observation table?
choices: No sound at all
Same
Higher
Lower
quiz.rationale: Moving a sound source towards a stationary listener gives a higher perceived pitch. This matches the approaching matatu horn. Students only record this at this stage and are not asked to explain it.
quiz.placement: Station A: PhET Sound Simulation observation table

quiz.prompt: The Station B diagram card shows the Kabete tunnel as about 8 m wide. The FM wavelength is about 2.9 m and the AM wavelength is about 300 m, all drawn to the same scale. Which statement is an accurate OBSERVATION from this card?
choices: Both the FM and AM wavelengths are shorter than the tunnel width
The FM wavelength is longer than the tunnel width, while the AM wavelength is shorter than the tunnel width
The FM and AM wavelengths are about the same size as each other
The FM wavelength is shorter than the tunnel width, while the AM wavelength is much longer than the tunnel width
quiz.rationale: 2.9 m is less than 8 m, and 300 m is far greater than 8 m. This is a measured comparison, which is exactly what the observation-only protocol asks students to record.

quiz.prompt: On the Station B card, the AM wavelength is about 300 m and the FM wavelength (Classic 105, 105.2 MHz) is about 2.9 m. Roughly how many times longer is the AM wavelength than the FM wavelength?
choices: About 870 times
About 38 times
About 103 times
About 10 times
quiz.rationale: 300 ÷ 2.9 ≈ 103, so the AM wavelength is roughly 100 times longer than the FM wavelength.

quiz.prompt: At the end of this first lesson, where does the class stand on why FM (Classic 105) cuts out in the Kabete tunnel while AM stays audible?
choices: It cannot ever be explained, because radio waves and sound are completely unrelated
It has been fully explained: Classic 105 simply has a weaker transmitter than the AM station
It is not yet fully explained: the class has noticed some patterns and listed what is still missing
It has been fully explained: the radio's FM setting switches itself off inside tunnels
quiz.rationale: In the convergence discussion the teacher names emerging patterns without endorsing any answer, and records what is 'still missing' as seeds for the DQB. The weaker-transmitter idea is the technological explanation the teacher steers groups away from.
quiz.placement: Convergence discussion and 'Link back to phenomenon'

quiz.prompt: For the Driving Question Board, the teacher asks each student to write ONE question they genuinely cannot yet answer, starting with HOW or WHY. Which sticky note best follows these instructions?
choices: Is Classic 105 the best radio station in Nairobi?
What time did the bus leave Nakuru?
Why does the pitch of the horn change only when the matatu is moving?
Did you enjoy the buzzer demonstration?
quiz.rationale: This question starts with 'Why', can be investigated and refers to a physical process (motion changing pitch). The teacher reads out this very question as an excellent example.
quiz.placement: DQB posting: 'The Horn Puzzle' and 'The Tunnel Puzzle' columns

quiz.prompt: Students draw an 'Initial Wave Model' showing a wave travelling from a matatu horn to an ear and then entering a narrow tunnel. What is the main purpose of this drawing?
choices: To give the final answer to the driving question
To produce a neat art project that will be marked for accuracy
To show their current thinking, which they will revise in later lessons as they gather evidence
To copy the correct wave shape that the teacher gives the class
quiz.rationale: Students are told their model 'does not need to be correct — it needs to show your current thinking' and that it will be revised in every lesson. The teacher does not correct wave shapes at this stage.
quiz.placement: Initial Wave Model drawing and pair comparison

quiz.prompt: The lesson describes both the sound of a matatu horn and the Classic 105 radio signal as waves. What does a wave carry from the horn to a listener's ear?
choices: Tiny pieces of the horn that break off and fly to the ear
Air from the horn that travels all the way to the ear
Nothing at all, because sound is not a wave
Energy, without the matter itself travelling from the horn to the ear
quiz.rationale: The knowledge outcome states that waves are disturbances that transfer energy without transferring matter. Air or pieces of the horn travelling to the ear is the common misconception.
quiz.placement: After the whole lesson (knowledge learning outcome)
